Incorporating the Beige Book insights into the March 21, 2018 FOMC assessment reinforces a constructive macro tone. The Beige Book points to broad employment growth and strong demand for qualified workers, with employers raising wages and compensation structures influenced by the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act. These reports align with the FOMC’s view of a strong labor market and lend support to inflation firming toward 2 percent. On credit, the SLOOS indicates easing for C&I lending to larger firms, which supports continued moderate expansion, while tighter terms and quality concerns in unsecured consumer credit and CRE highlight localized risks. Net effect: outlook remains moderately positive with gradual hikes appropriate; risks are balanced but include labor-supply constraints and pockets of credit tightening in consumer and CRE. Given the Beige Book’s stronger labor and wage signals, the tone tilts slightly more positive than before.
